subject: social
title: Families and Cultures
about: Families come in many shapes, and every family has a culture: the foods, music, languages, clothing and celebrations it shares, and learning about other families' traditions with respect. NC 1.B.1.1 (cultural practices and traditions) and 1.B.1.2 (how people of different cultures shape a community).
tip: At dinner, name one food, song or word that comes from your family's culture and ask him to pick one from a friend's.

cards.q: The people who love you and take care of you at home are your...
cards.note: Families can be big or small. Every family is different.

cards.q: Leo lives with his grandma. Mia lives with her mom and dad. Who has a family?
cards.note: A family is the people who care for you, whoever they are.

cards.q: Ava has a stepdad and two stepbrothers. Those people are part of her...
cards.note: When grown-ups marry, their families join together.

cards.q: Your mom's mom or your dad's mom is your...
cards.note: Grandma, Nana and Abuela are all names for a grandmother.

cards.q: Your aunt's child or your uncle's child is your...
cards.note: Cousins are family too. Many cousins play together at family parties.

cards.q: The words a family uses to talk, like English or Spanish, are their...
cards.note: Thousands of languages are spoken around the world.

cards.q: Zoe speaks Spanish at home and English at school. How many languages does she speak?
cards.note: Knowing two languages is called being bilingual.

cards.q: Hola means hello in which language?
cards.note: Many families in North Carolina speak Spanish at home.

cards.q: Tacos, sushi and pizza each started in a different...
cards.note: Tacos come from Mexico, sushi from Japan and pizza from Italy.

cards.q: A kimono from Japan and a sari from India are special kinds of...
cards.note: Many families wear special clothes for holidays and celebrations.

cards.q: Which of these is part of a family's culture?
cards.note: Songs, dances and stories are passed down in families.

cards.q: The Mexican hat dance and Irish step dance are two kinds of...
cards.note: Many cultures have their own special dances.

cards.q: A new friend eats a food that is new to you. What is a kind thing to do?
cards.note: Asking kind questions is a great way to learn about a new culture.

cards.q: Ben's friend invites him to a Lunar New Year dinner. What can Ben learn there?
cards.note: Going to a friend's celebration is a fun way to learn about their culture.

cards.q: All families, big or small, give their kids what?
cards.note: Families look different, but they all take care of each other.

cards.q: How can you share your family's culture with your class?
cards.note: You could bring a food, teach a word or show a photo.

cards.q: A classmate's family celebrates a holiday that is new to you. What can you say?
cards.note: Everyone's traditions are special. Kind words show respect.
Your family's foods, words and celebrations are your culture.
